# Assignment Operation Journal

> Riido task: RIID-4669

Executable SSOT: [`assignment-operation-journal.riido.json`](assignment-operation-journal.riido.json).

## Ownership

`internal/riidoaiserver` owns the journal port, claim port, lease/projection shapes, and replay reducer contract.

## Evidence Loop

| Step | Statement |
| --- | --- |
| Observe | Stable event keys previously deduplicated only local event history and fallback inventory reads could occupy the global assignment actor after caller cancellation. |
| Hypothesis | Private bounded ACK receipts committed by projection CAS and cancellable candidate preflight outside the actor preserve retry identity and stop responsiveness across replicas. |
| Execute | Generate the reader doc and exercise replica/restart/CAS replay, changed-payload refusal, legacy repair preservation and cancellation/stop races before journal verification. |
| Evaluate | The journal verifier checks owning ports, source anchors and generated freshness; focused tests require exact original ACKs, no duplicate side effects and actor responsiveness during inventory stalls. |
| Retrospective | Ready and terminal ACK guarantees cover newly committed stable-key receipts; legacy records without receipts retain compatibility and cannot retroactively prove a lost original acknowledgement. |

## Ports

| Name | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `AssignmentOperationStore` | append assignment mutation records |
| `AssignmentOperationLoader` | load durable records for replay |
| `AssignmentQueueReader` | read queued assignments by agent |
| `AssignmentClaimer` | atomically claim next assignment |
| `AssignmentActiveLeaseStore` | load and refresh active assignment leases |
| `AssignmentProjectionReader` | load assignment read projections |

## Records

| Name | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `AssignmentOperationRecord` | append-only mutation plus emitted task events |
| `AssignmentProjection` | durable assignment read projection with private CAS-preserved bounded recovery and Ready/terminal ACK receipts; receipts never appear in public Assignment JSON |
| `AssignmentActiveLease` | active assignment lease snapshot |
| `AssignmentClaimResult` | claim outcome plus operation evidence |

## Replay Rules

| Rule | Kind | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `validate-before-apply` | replay | validate every operation record before applying it |
| `stable-replay-order` | replay | order by last event sequence, recorded_at, then operation_id |
| `dedupe-task-events` | replay | dedupe events by task_id and sequence |
| `cross-task-same-seq` | replay | keep same sequence events when task_id differs |
| `track-next-sequences` | replay | rebuild next_event_seq and next_assignment_seq |
| `sort-replayed-events` | replay | sort task event histories by sequence |
| `rebuild-current-assignment` | index | rebuild task current_assignment_id from newest assignment ordering |
| `rebuild-agent-index` | index | rebuild agent assignment lists in assignment creation order |
| `durable-daemon-event-ack` | replay | For stable-key Ready and terminal events, atomically persist at most eight private hashed payload receipts with the operation and projection. Identical retries across replicas or restart restore the original event ACK and assignment acknowledgement fields without another event, outbox, log or span; reject semantic payload reuse and fail closed at the bound without evicting a receipt. A Ready ACK can authorize dispatch only while the current execution is still leased/ready with the same unexpired lease; Running, cancelling and terminal executions refuse it. The private receipt JSON is bounded to 16 KiB and validated before any durable write; the cap never evicts an original receipt. |
| `candidate-preflight-outside-actor` | index | Run selected fallback inventory authorization outside the assignment actor under caller cancellation and a two-second bound. The actor and each projection CAS retry recheck the observed assignment fingerprint, execution binding, active lease, state and request context; an intervening stop or lease/policy generation change invalidates approval. |
| `daemon-event-dependency-status` | replay | Ready, recovery journal and terminal event persistence failures remain retryable: dependency unavailability or exhausted CAS returns 503, deadline 504 and cancellation 408 with fixed messages. Input validation stays 400. A daemon retries the same stable event key within its existing finite budget; storage failures never authorize dispatch. Legacy snapshot-only and write-only journal event paths mutate a private trial and publish or retain ACKs only after their single authority accepts persistence. A non-projection legacy journal combined with a snapshot store has no atomic receipt port and fails closed before either write; production projection-backed journals and local snapshot-only mode remain supported. Stale Ready/recovery lease rechecks have a two-second total lookup deadline, including operation-store actor queueing; timeout is retryable 504 and never publishes or caches an ACK. This bounds the existing background lookup but does not claim caller-context propagation through all actor operations. |
| `authenticated-execution-claim-provenance` | replay | Device-authenticated claims retain immutable device, owner-at-claim, assignment requester and hashed lease epoch in the same CAS as lease/projection/journal writes. Covered claims additionally bind server-issued coverage/credential generations and server-validated runtime termination scope. Replay and snapshots retain original provenance across credential rotation, stale repair and ordinary terminal events. Legacy bearer claims retain unknown provenance and must condition-check their trusted binding as uncovered in the actual claim transaction. Claim history alone never grants permission; the complete-coverage installation policy owns that separate verdict. |
| `claim-local-termination-receipt` | replay | Device-authenticated local invocation observations bind the immutable original claim owner, device and hashed epoch. Store one immutable receipt per epoch through claim, projection and receipt conditions plus one bounded device-policy revision advance in a four-action transaction. Existing receipt replay only checks its three immutable guards without advancing revision. A same-epoch active projection conflicts before either a new receipt or a replay ACK; missing or legacy unhashed projections fail closed. Compare the current projection lease_epoch hash with its actual token digest and CAS it with schema, state and sequence, without copying raw lease or prompt into conditions. Different current epochs permit only the old receipt and never mutate the new execution. Up to three attempts within the request deadline reread all guards and recover only the exact committed ACK; changed counts conflict. The count measures provider Process.Start successes, not host commands or OS descendants. Snapshot-only mode persists a private trial before ACK; unsupported journal authorities fail closed. No projection, active lease, task journal, SSE, outbox or TTL mutation and no access permission or remote completion inference. |
| `installation-policy-revision-fence` | replay | Authenticated claim admission, new termination receipts and new installation links atomically advance the bounded device-policy revision. Legacy/local history remains unknown unless a current matching unexpired non-owner lease proves blocked. Only a new server-issued dcov_ namespace born atomically with its credential/device/CURRENT publication has complete coverage; re-enrollment, version, empty history and lease expiry never upgrade legacy. Every covered claim, read-only resume and Ready validates authenticated owner, coverage generation and current credential at its final CAS. Raw bearer claims require a trusted legacy binding and an uncovered-policy CAS; missing binding cannot claim. A non-owner or unknown-requester claim increments unresolved executions with the immutable claim and lease transaction. A new matching local-invocation receipt decrements once with claim, projection and ledger CAS; replay does not decrement, remote/unobserved receipts do not resolve, and an old epoch cannot close a new epoch. Current credential rotation may close an original claim without rewriting its provenance. Service policy rechecks immutable link, current credential authority and the same revision; allowed requires complete coverage and zero unresolved executions at that final authorization snapshot. It does not lock the whole response against later claims. Missing/corrupt authority, partial history, unsupported backends and unresolved restart stay unknown. Retry at most three times within two seconds. New covered enrollment is default-off until every poll-serving instance enforces these gates. Flag-off never removes existing enforcement; an unaware old binary is not a safe rollback. Legacy recovery, remote termination, monolith consumption and authenticated rollout remain separate acceptance gates. |
